1.explanation: This minimal React application uses the Carbon <Dropdown> component and forces it into the open state by leveraging the `downshiftProps.isOpen` property. When you load this component in Firefox on macOS and run the IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker, you will observe the same violation: none of the elements with role="option" are individually tabbable. They all receive `tabindex="-1"` and rely on arrow‐key navigation instead of Tab, triggering the critical violation reported in the bug.
1.bug_scenario: When a Carbon <Dropdown> is opened (either by clicking the toggle or by forcing it open via Downshift props), the list of <ListBoxMenuItem> elements all render with role="option" but none of these option elements are individually tabbable. Focus remains on the toggle button and keyboard navigation between options is handled internally by Downshift via arrow keys—not via the tab key. The IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker flags this as a violation (“None of the descendant elements with ‘option’ role is tabbable”).
